method_notes: Offset -11 (pdf 38 = folio 27; pdf 104 = folio 93). Q: q1-8 pdf38, q9-18 pdf39, q19-43 pdf40, q44-50 pdf41. A: keys 1-29 pdf104, 30-43 pdf105, 44-48 pdf106, 49-50 pdf107.

Sections: I MCQ q1-20; II one word/sentence q21-38 (vsa); III two/three q39-44 (sa); IV five/six q45-48 (la); V seven/eight q49-50 (la, header prints '(4 Marks)' -> marks=4 section_header set by add_stimuli_13).

FIGURES (read-the-diagram, question-side stimulus, added by add_stimuli_13): q12 'The diagram indicates' -> stimulus figure pdf39 (concentric isobars, arrows spiralling inward to a low-pressure centre labelled in Kannada = cyclonic circulation; key D cyclonic winds); q20 'type of rainfall shown in the given diagram' -> stimulus figure pdf40 (mountain cross-section, windward cloud+rain, leeward rain shadow, captioned 'Orographic rainfall'; key B orographic). Each: question asset role 'figure' + stimulus_id.

MCQ letter/text DISAGREEMENTS (no asserted answer, 'key text not among options', review): q3 key letter C but text 'Roaring Forties' = option A exactly (auto); q13 letter A text 'Temperate zone' matches no option (KEYNULL; letter A=Stratosphere); q16 letter B text 'Temperate zone' matches no option (KEYNULL; letter B=Stratosphere).

MCQ benign 'key text differs from option by a printed typo' (letter kept): q5 ('Wind compass' vs 'Wind vane'), q11 ('Due to extremely high temperature' vs 'Very high temperature'), q12 ('Cyclones' vs 'Cyclonic winds'), q14 ('Cumulus rain clouds' vs 'Cumulonimbus clouds' - ambiguous vs option B 'Cumulus clouds', letter D kept), q15 ('In the equatorial region' vs 'Equatorial region'), q19 ('Northern sub-tropical' vs 'North subtropical'). q1-2,4,6-10,17-18,20 exact.
q11 REVIEW (factual doubt, key kept): key says ionization due to 'extremely high temperature' (letter C); ionization is physically by UV absorption (option B). Printed key kept verbatim (v2 5.7).
q29 'key text does not address question' (review-blocking): key defines cyclones, question asks periodic winds. Kept verbatim.

VSA q21-38 answer.value = sentence verbatim. SA/LA SUB heading(s) + steps: q39=1, q40=1, q41=1, q42=1, q43=4, q45=1, q46=1, q47=2, q48=6, q49=7, q50=8 (two headings). BUL q44=4. q45 'astemperature' typo kept; q49 'extremely feel the low temperature' typo kept; q50 belts de-conflated (OCR ran 'Northern Subpolar...Southern' together).
q40 stem OCR garble '( .(E)' -> cleaned to '(E)'. q3 '40 degree' (OCR degree symbol). MARKS none printed in sections I-IV; section V '(4 Marks)'.

stimuli.text: A diagram of concentric circular isobars with arrows spiralling inward toward a central low-pressure area (the centre is labelled in Kannada). It depicts cyclonic wind circulation; the student identifies the type of wind shown.

A labelled cross-section of a mountain: moist air rises the windward slope forming cloud and rain, while descending air warms and forms a rain shadow on the leeward side. The figure is captioned 'Orographic rainfall'. The student identifies the type of rainfall shown.

questions.text: What are the causes for temperature inversion?
questions.text_as_printed: What are the causes for temperature inversion? (A)

answer.value:
Inversion of temperature:
In certain conditions, the temperature decreases with altitude in the atmosphere this Phenomenon is called astemperature inversion. It occurs in mountainous valley regions due to prolonged nights, clear cloudless skies, dry air, calm winds, and snow-covered mountain peaks.

questions.text: What are clouds? Name their types.

answer.value:
Clouds:

questions.text: Write a note on weather and climate.
questions.text_as_printed: Write a note on weather and climate. (A)

answer.value:
Weather and Climate:
Weather refers to the short-term atmospheric conditions of a place, e.g., cloudy, sunny, or clear weather. The scientific study of weather is called meteorology.
Climate refers to the long-term atmospheric conditions of a region, e.g., equatorial or desert climate. The scientific study of climate is called climatology.

questions.text: Write about the structure of the atmosphere.
questions.text_as_printed: Write about the structure of the atmosphere. (A)

answer.value:
Composition and Structure of the Atmosphere:
The atmosphere is a mixture of various gases, dust particles, and water vapor.
Nitrogen, oxygen, argon, carbon dioxide, and ozone are found in atmosphere
The atmosphere is divided into five layers.
The Troposphere, the lowest layer, experiences all weather changes, with decreasing temperature and pressure as altitude increases.
The Stratosphere, the second layer, contains ozone, which absorbs harmful ultraviolet rays, protecting life on Earth.
The Mesosphere, the third layer, has extremely feel the low temperature
The Ionosphere (Thermosphere) has high temperature, and air molecules ionize, hence the name is Ionosphere.
The Exosphere, the outermost layer, has very low pressure.

questions.text: What is atmospheric pressure? Name the major pressure belts of the world.
questions.text_as_printed: What is atmospheric pressure? Name the major pressure belts of the world. (E)

answer.value:
Atmospheric Pressure and Pressure Belts:
Air has weight and exerts pressure on the Earth's surface, known as atmospheric pressure.
Major pressure belts include:
Equatorial Low-Pressure Belt
Northern Subtropical High-Pressure Belt
Southern Subtropical High-Pressure Belt
Northern Subpolar Low-Pressure Belt
Southern Subpolar Low-Pressure Belt
Northern Polar High-Pressure Belt
Southern Polar High-Pressure Belt
